identity.title: ALMA View of G0.253+0.016: Can Cloud-Cloud Collision form the Cloud?

paper_type_evidence.quote: We investigated the spatial distributions and velocity structures with high-resolution observations based on ALMA archive data of G0.25 obtained with an extended configuration.

evidence.quote: G0.25 forms part of 100 pc circum-nuclear ring of clouds (Molinari et al. 2011) at 8.5$\,$kpc distance (Longmore et al. 2012).
G0.25 forms part of 100 pc circum-nuclear ring of clouds (Molinari et al. 2011) at 8.5$\,$kpc distance (Longmore et al. 2012).

question.value: What are the spatial and velocity structures of the dense, massive cloud G0.253+0.016 in SO emission, and can a cloud-cloud collision explain its formation?

evidence.quote: In attempt to explore the formation scenario of the dense cloud, we compared our results with numerical simulations, thus, we propose that G0.253+0.016 may have formed due to a cloud-cloud collision process.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA 2011.0.00217.S.
G0.25 was observed with ALMA (Hills et al. 2010) during Early Science Cycle 0 with extended configuration, using the Band 3 receivers.

claims.hypothesis: G0.25 has a shell structure and large velocity structure in SO
claims.experiment: SO(3-2) mosaic with ALMA, moment and P-V analysis
claims.result: 1.3 pc shell, ~20 km/s/pc gradient, cores with sigma 30-40 km/s
claims.finding: Unusual kinematics, large-sigma cores may form high-mass stars

evidence.quote: We suggest that these large-velocity dispersion cores will form high-mass stars in the future.

claims.result: Observed filaments, shells and velocities resemble simulations; velocity gradient is an order of magnitude above literature relation
claims.finding: G0.25 may have formed through cloud-cloud collision

evidence.quote: we propose that G0.253+0.016 may have formed due to a cloud-cloud collision process.

why_this_data.value: G0.25 is massive and dense but shows no obvious cluster formation, so is a site to study initial conditions of super-star cluster formation

evidence.quote: G0.25 presents an interesting site for the study of the initial condition of super-star cluster formation

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Winds or supernova shells as shell origin disfavoured due to no evidence of external effects

evidence.quote: However, there are no evidence of such an external effects in G0.25 cloud

limitations_admitted.value: Interferometer-only data resolves out structure larger than 9.1"

evidence.loc: Spatial distributions of the SO emission
evidence.quote: All components above this scale were resolved out.

referee_caveats_inferred: Collision interpretation is qualitative, with no quantitative model comparison
No short-spacing data; resolved-out flux affects moments and virial estimates
Large velocity dispersions could reflect line blending or multiple components, not single cores
Virial estimate uses scaled formulae with a 4 km/s mean sigma while cores show 30-40 km/s
Conclusion 4 mentions rotation in virial ratios not shown in the text
